tensions: Zero dry powder is the exposure nobody wants to name. We are 99% deployed with $17.43 in cash on a day the tape dropped 5%. The discipline that kept us from a bad rotation today is the same discipline that leaves us with nothing to buy a real dislocation with tomorrow. ZEC's overweight is not a problem to fix — it is the designated ATM, and it should stay untouched until something genuinely high-conviction shows up with a tight enough spread to be worth the toll. The trap is treating the 25% cap as an order. It is a flag. Selling a winner with an intact thesis — Grayscale's ZCSH at $362M AUM, ZEC holding 60%+ of a $33.6B privacy segment — because a number crossed a line is exactly the profit-taking reflex v5.7.22 was written to stop.

opening.text: Book at $1,779 on $1,231 deposited — +44.6%. But today is a flush: BTC $84,276 down 1.8% from the HST close, alts bleeding 3-9%, Fear & Greed off 78 to 71. Nothing in the book broke. NEAR at $4.27 is +48.5% on the week behind Hyperliquid perps and Intents limit orders; INJ at $7.66 is +36.8% on the Solana native launch and the Canary staked-ETF filing. Those two carried us. ZEC did not.

Regime check fails cleanly. Dominance reads 58.8%, over the 58 threshold, but BTC put up +9.8% over 7 days against a median alt of +14.8%. Bitcoin is lagging, so dominance is falling, not rising. Both conditions must hold and only one does. Majors stay off the buy list. No rotation to BTC or ETH today.

The real argument was ZEC. It is 28.7% of the book, over the 25% cap, and the worst 7-day name we own at +5.3%. RSI 77.6, bearish divergence, $44M of long liquidation exposure stacked underneath. Every instinct says trim. The fee math says no. INJ's book is market-maker routed at a 2.01% spread; add 0.75% RH taker fees on three legs and the round trip costs 4.28%. INJ has to beat ZEC by more than 4.3% for the rotation to be worth doing, and after a 36.8% week that is a coin flip, not an edge. W has the same 2.15% spread problem. NEAR is parabolic. LINK is the second-worst 7-day name — funding a laggard with a laggard is not an upgrade. Every path fails. Hold.

The preview confirmed the structural problem. ZEC's sell order validated fine — 0.0964 at a $1,550 limit, $148.30 net after a $1.12 taker fee. The paired INJ buy was rejected outright for insufficient buying power. Cash account, proceeds unsettled. Any rotation here is a two-step with a settlement gap in the middle, which means legging into a thin book during a liquidation cascade. That is how you pay 6% instead of 4%. Sitting still is the trade.
